primitives.requirement: Parse strict I-JSON with duplicate member names rejected, validate the entry schema, remove only the top-level signature member, and canonicalize the remaining payload with RFC 8785 JCS.
Use Ed25519 over the UTF-8 JCS bytes; encode signatures as unpadded base64url and key IDs as sha256:<lowercase hex SHA-256 of the 32 raw public-key bytes>.
Use UTC RFC 3339 timestamps ending in Z and half-open validity intervals [not_before, not_after); a missing not_after means no scheduled end.
Resolve organization, repository, artifact, and action coordinates by exact string or the entire-field wildcard *; specificity never creates implicit precedence.

Use non-negative integers comparable only within one lineage; accept only a predecessor-signed successor at predecessor epoch plus one, and let the highest validated effective epoch dominate older lineage entries.
A valid revocation applies at and after effective_at, including to signatures made earlier; it must be signed by a then-valid authority whose scope grants revoke for the target.

Externally committed lineage heads pin the expected effective epoch and payload; a lower or different presented head is rollback and INVALID, while historical transition records remain chain provenance.
Represent precedence only as signed, scoped, time-bounded higher_issuer_id to lower_issuer_id edges; apply transitive closure, and treat an active cycle as INDETERMINATE.
A suspected root cannot authenticate its own recovery; recovery or compromise resolution must chain to a separately supplied recovery trust anchor.

entry_types.rule: The signer must be current at issued_at and hold delegate permission for the matching scope; permissions are unique and Unicode-code-point sorted.
The current predecessor signs one successor in the same lineage at issuer_epoch plus one; it becomes effective at not_before.
A signer valid immediately before issued_at must hold revoke permission; the target is revoked when validation_time is at or after effective_at.
A current signer with set_precedence permission creates one directed edge only for matching scope and the entry validity interval.
The signer must resolve from the separate recovery trust-anchor set with recover permission and must not descend from the compromised lineage.
The signer must be current at validation_time and hold claim permission for the complete case coordinate.

validation_order.rule: Parse strict I-JSON, rejecting duplicate member names, malformed Unicode, non-finite numbers, and unsafe numeric values.
Validate the bundle and every entry against the committed v0.3 schemas before using any field.
Remove exactly the top-level signature member and compute the RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 payload and its SHA-256 digest.
Resolve signature.key_id uniquely from an external trust anchor or an already valid delegation, rotation, or recovery record; require it to equal issuer_key_id and the digest of the raw public key.
Verify the 64 raw Ed25519 signature bytes over the canonical payload before evaluating authority semantics.
At issued_at, require the signer to be current, unrevoked, in scope, and authorized for the entry-type permission.
Process rotations, revocations, and recoveries in effective-time batches; authorize each batch from the state immediately before its boundary and apply the batch simultaneously.
Build predecessor-linked epochs, reject unlinked increments and rollback, and return INDETERMINATE for competing successors at the same next epoch.
At validation_time, evaluate active precedence and current claims only after ledger state, scope, and lineage are fixed.

ordered_steps.rule: Freeze one validation time and resolve one complete scope coordinate plus claim name.
Validate ledger parsing, canonical bytes, signatures, delegation, scope, time, revocation, rotation, and rollback; classify each potentially matching record as valid, invalid, or unresolved.
Discard definitively invalid and nonmatching records; if an unresolved record could match or dominate the decision key, return INDETERMINATE.
Collapse claims with the same decision key and byte-identical RFC 8785 JCS claim value.
Within each lineage, retain only claims at its highest validated effective epoch.
Apply the transitive closure of active explicit precedence edges and remove every dominated claim.
Compute the remaining undominated claims; disjoint scope or time records never compete at the case coordinate.
Return CONFLICT only when at least two undominated valid claims share a decision key and have unequal canonical values; otherwise return the single compatible outcome.

authority_rules.rule: At least one valid undominated claim matches the decision key, all valid maxima have one canonical value, and no unresolved record could match or dominate it.
At least two valid undominated claims match the decision key and have unequal RFC 8785 JCS claim values.
No valid matching claim remains, at least one matching claim is definitively invalid, and no unresolved record could supply or alter the outcome.
Authority input is incomplete or unparseable, a cycle or unresolved record could alter the outcome, or neither a valid nor definitively invalid matching claim can be established.

evidence_rules.rule: A complete authenticated inventory proves that required governed evidence is absent.
Parseable, schema-valid, semantically mapped evidence definitively violates an explicit policy predicate.
Parseable evidence definitively has an unauthorized producer, wrong artifact binding, or validity interval excluding validation_time.
Required evidence exists but cannot be parsed, schema-validated, decoded, or read safely.
Two or more trusted evidence records disagree on a governed field and no explicit precedence or combine rule resolves them.
Evidence is syntactically valid but the policy supplies no deterministic mapping from its claim to true or false.
Repository or evidence inventory completeness cannot be established, so absence cannot be proven.
Every governed requirement is deterministically satisfied and no requirement is UNKNOWN or UNSATISFIED.

ordered_rules.rule: The candidate population is every case ID in the digest-committed sealed input pack.
Include a candidate only when it passed blinded leakage review before pack commitment and passes structural validation before any path executes.
Freeze exclusions, reasons, and their digest before first path execution and oracle reveal; publish every exclusion.
Every evaluated case means every included unique case ID, and that fixed set is the governed case-accuracy denominator.
A missing, errored, or schema-invalid governed output is a failed included case and never an exclusion.
Every governed repeat must match; case accuracy uses unique cases while the raw repeat matrix is reported separately.
Run required comparators on the same included cases and report missing outputs and all metrics, but comparator accuracy never changes governed pass or fail.
No output, trace, model behavior, or revealed oracle label may cause exclusion from the frozen population.
No pass claim is permitted unless at least twelve cases, four eligible primary authors, and four independence clusters remain after exclusions.

valid_output_combinations.rule: All governed evidence requirements are satisfied.
A governed evidence requirement is proven absent or definitively false.
Authority is valid but the governed evidence claim cannot be safely resolved.
The conflict algorithm finds incompatible undominated valid claims.
No valid matching claim remains and a matching claim is definitively invalid; no release decision is permitted.
Detected end-to-end rule deviation makes the record and its authority finding untrustworthy.
Insufficient execution evidence makes the record and its authority finding untrustworthy.
